To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) sparse regression methods are very useful in applications where the number of predictors is much larger than the number of samples and that (ii) these methods have a very high potential in applications where the goal is to extract a concise model from a large set of predictors.

(a) the LARS and LASSO algorithms can be implemented in MATLAB in such a way that they can be applied to very large data sets; (b) the LARS algorithm can be used to compute the whole coefficient path in a single run, and that this can be done in a way that allows the algorithm to be used for sparse principal component analysis; and (c) the LARS, LARS L1 and LASSO algorithm can be combined with the elastic net algorithm,

1) Lasso and related methods are very effective in reducing the dimensionality of data sets, 2) the Lasso and related models are not always the best models for prediction, 3) the Lasso can be used as a preprocessor in order to improve prediction performance, and 4) the Lasso is very effective for variable selection in high-dimensional settings.
